thread:
Priyom Das: quick q — getting tripped up in demos explaining Dedicated commits vs hosted usage-based. Prospect asked “so do I pay twice?” when I said they can start hosted then move to Dedicated. What’s the clean talk track?

Avery Johnson: +1. I keep saying “reserved capacity” but then they ask if tokens are still billed. I don’t want to misstate.

Soojin Lee: Here’s the simplest framing we’ve been using:
- Hosted API = metered usage (pay for what you consume: tokens/embeddings). Great for fast start + variable workloads.
- Dedicated = you reserve a slice of capacity (GPU pool) for predictable throughput / isolation. Commercially it’s a commit (monthly/annual) for that reserved capacity.
- You’re not “paying twice” for the same traffic. It’s two different SKUs depending on where traffic runs.

Soojin Lee: Language that’s worked for me:
“Hosted is like a meter. Dedicated is like reserving your own lane on the highway. Same API, but Dedicated buys you predictability and isolation.”

Camila Reyes: +1 to Soojin. Also helpful to say: “Most customers start on hosted, then we move the steady baseline to Dedicated once they know their throughput requirements.” It makes it feel like a progression vs. an add-on.

Priyom Das: ok but what about hybrid? (they want baseline dedicated, burst on hosted)

Soojin Lee: Yup, mention it explicitly, but keep it high level:
- Dedicated handles baseline / SLO-sensitive routes
- Hosted can be used for burst/overflow, experiments, or secondary regions
We should avoid getting into rate cards live unless they ask.

Markus Klein: from the SE side: I usually say “same control plane + console; routing policy decides where requests go.” Then if they ask billing: “Each request is billed under the capacity it uses.”

Avery Johnson: what’s the one sentence if procurement is on the call?

Stephanie Nguyen: “Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is a contract for reserved capacity with predictable performance. You choose which one per workload.” If they push on numbers, park it and say we’ll follow up with a written quote.

Camila Reyes: Also: don’t say “unlimited tokens” for Dedicated. It’s capacity-based; we size it to target TPS/latency. People hear unlimited and it creates cleanup later.

Priyom Das: makes sense. Do we have an internal doc I can link/skim before next call?

Soojin Lee: Yep — pricing enablement doc has the exact wording + guardrails + credits guidance:
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SE/ Demo+Pricing+and+Credits+Guidance
(If you can’t access, DM me.)

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: thank you. I’ll adopt the “meter vs reserved lane” line.

Markus Klein: Also FYI if someone asks “what do I get for Dedicated besides predictability?” anchor on: isolation/noisy neighbor, pinned model versions/rollouts, custom autoscaling policy, and SLA options.

Stephanie Nguyen: If you get stuck mid-call, drop a note in #sales with the company + who’s on the line. We can jump in with the right wording. Reactions: :white_check_mark:
